2608.01456.title: Long-Horizon Embodied Decision-Making via Multimodal Memory Compression
2608.01456.paper_summary: Agents are increasingly expected to act not only as task executors, but also as decision-makers on behalf of human users. This shift requires agents to accumulate evidence over long horizons, interpret implicit user preferences, and compare multiple candidates under partial observations. In this work, we propose DunphyBench, a new benchmark for evaluating agents on long-horizon human-centered embodied decision-making, where the agent must navigate through multiple embodied housing environments and make decisions that align with multi-dimensional human preferences. Unlike standard embodied reasoning tasks that often focus on procedural planning or immediate goal completion, our setting requires agents to integrate multimodal, multi-source input into coherent knowledge that supports complex reasoning across long horizon. The evaluation results reveal that there is a substantial gap between current agents and human performance. Furthermore, our diagnosis of state-of-the-art VLM-driven agents reveals that memory management is one of the bottlenecks, where raw multimodal history introduces noise that hinders decision quality. Motivated by this finding, we design MeMento, a preference-conditioned multimodal memory compressor that selectively compresses decision-relevant information from long-horizon history based on user preferences with a fixed set of memory tokens. Experiments show that MeMento helps VLM-driven agents improve accuracy by 7.18%, while reducing memory usage by 85.38% compared to the strongest baseline.
2608.01456.paper_summary_zh: 代理人越來越被期望不僅僅是任務執行者，還要作為人類用戶的決策者。這一轉變要求代理人在長期內積累證據，解釋隱含的用戶偏好，並在部分觀察下比較多個候選者。在這項工作中，我們提出了DunphyBench，一個新的基準，用於評估代理人在長期以人為中心的具身決策中，代理人必須在多個具身住房環境中導航，並做出符合多維人類偏好的決策。與通常專注於程序規劃或立即目標完成的標準具身推理任務不同，我們的設置要求代理人將多模態、多來源的輸入整合成連貫的知識，以支持跨越長期的複雜推理。評估結果顯示，目前的代理人與人類表現之間存在顯著差距。此外，我們對最先進的VLM驅動代理人的診斷顯示，記憶管理是其中一個瓶頸，原始的多模態歷史引入的噪聲妨礙了決策質量。受到這一發現的啟發，我們設計了MeMento，一種基於用戶偏好的偏好條件多模態記憶壓縮器，根據固定的記憶標記集選擇性地壓縮來自長期歷史的與決策相關的信息。實驗表明，MeMento幫助VLM驅動的代理人提高了7.18%的準確性，同時與最強基準相比減少了85.38%的記憶使用。
